title: Emrys and the Archive
premise: Xanthe Nakamura, a clone of a murdered diplomat, has spent ten years hauling cargo through contested orbits, hiding from the war that killed his original. When he intercepts a distress signal in a language extinct for two centuries — the tongue of the Archive, a vanished civilization whose jump-gate technology both sides covet — he becomes the only living being who can decode it. Hunted by the Republic fleet and the insurgent Concord alike, Xanthe assembles a ragtag crew of outcasts who become the family he never let himself want. The message turns out to be the Archive's last testament: proof that the war's founding atrocity was staged by the Republic's own admiralty. In the climax, Xanthe must broadcast it from the heart of the contested jump gate before the window closes, choosing to end his anonymity and claim his original's unfinished work; the truth ends the war but costs him his ship and nearly his life, and he survives not as a copy of someone else, but as himself.
about_author: Wren Thornbury is the pen name of a former orbital logistics analyst who spent six years writing stories in shipping manifests before turning to fiction. They live somewhere with unreliable gravity and excellent tea.

chapters.title: Dead Language, Live Signal
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Hauling scrap through the Kestrel Verge, Xanthe's aging freighter catches a repeating signal in a language his original once studied — one extinct for two centuries. He should ignore it. Instead he records it, hands shaking, and feels for the first time in ten years like someone is watching him.

chapters.title: The Man Who Was Murdered
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, flashback-woven. Docked at Ceres Hollow, Xanthe decrypts fragments using memories that aren't his — inherited linguistic instincts from the original Nakamura. A Republic patrol scans his ship; he realizes the signal pinged their network too. Someone else heard it, and they're coming.

chapters.title: Crew of Strays
chapters.summary: POV rotating: engineer Dessa Okonkwo, disgraced medic Ruel, and teenage stowaway Pip each get a scene revealing why they signed onto a clone's ghost ship. Xanthe tells them nothing about the signal, then immediately breaks his own rule when the patrol boards. Dessa covers for him without asking why.

chapters.title: What the Original Left Behind
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. In a dead-drop locker on Titan Annex, Xanthe finds his original's hidden research: the Archive civilization didn't die out — they were erased, and the diplomat was killed for proving it. The message isn't a distress call. It's an accusation, addressed to whoever could read it.

chapters.title: Republic Shadows
chapters.summary: POV Admiral Sera Voss, antagonist introduction. Voss receives orders to recover 'asset NAKAMURA-2' alive and erase everything else. She's a true believer beginning to doubt. Her interrogation of a captured Concord courier reveals the insurgents also decoded part of the signal — and are racing to the same coordinates.

chapters.title: Running the Verge
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. A chase sequence through debris fields as the crew outruns a Republic corvette. Ruel takes shrapnel saving Pip; Xanthe flies a maneuver only the original could have flown, and hates how good it feels. They escape, barely, into the uncharted Drift.

chapters.title: The Concord's Offer
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Insurgent captain Ilsa Reyes boards under parley flag: join us, translate the message, and we'll give you a new identity far from the war. Xanthe almost says yes — until he realizes Reyes wants to weaponize the revelation, not end the war with it. He refuses. It costs them their fuel reserves.

chapters.title: Lessons in a Dead Tongue
chapters.summary: POV Pip. The youngest crew member asks Xanthe to teach her the Archive language, and through teaching he finally confronts what he is: not a copy, but a continuation. Quiet character chapter; Dessa and Ruel patch the ship and each other. First real laughter aboard since chapter one.

chapters.title: Gate of Ghosts
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. They reach the Drift's edge and find it: an intact Archive jump gate, dormant for two centuries, humming with the same signal. Decoded fully at last, the message names the admiralty officials who staged the atrocity that started the war — and offers the gate itself as proof.

chapters.title: Voss Descends
chapters.summary: POV Admiral Voss. Ordered to destroy the gate rather than let either side hold it, Voss begins quietly falsifying her own logs. Her aide notices. Meanwhile the Concord fleet mobilizes toward the Drift, tipped off by the traitor inside Voss's command — setting three forces on collision course.

chapters.title: The Traitor Aboard
chapters.summary: POV Ruel. The medic discovers someone aboard has been transmitting their position. Suspicion tears at the crew; Dessa accuses Pip, who breaks down. The real leak is Ruel himself — coerced months ago with his sister's safety. He confesses to Xanthe alone, expecting to be spaced.

chapters.title: Judgment Call
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Crew tribunal over Ruel. Xanthe argues that power over another person's life is exactly what corrupted the admiralty — and votes to keep Ruel aboard, chained to making amends. Dessa storms out. The family fractures precisely when they need each other most.

chapters.title: Concord Vanguard
chapters.summary: POV Ilsa Reyes. The Concord strike force reaches the gate first and begins rigging it to broadcast a doctored version of the message — one blaming the Republic wholesale, enough to justify total war. Reyes justifies it to herself in chillingly reasonable terms. Power's corruption, mirrored.

chapters.title: Into the Gate
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Using the Archive language as a key, the crew slips past the gate's dormant defenses while Concord engineers work outside. Inside, they find the Archive's final vault: recordings, archives, the whole murdered civilization's testimony. Pip realizes the Archive chose to be understood, not feared.

chapters.title: Two Hundred Years of Silence
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, interwoven with Archive testimony. The vault reveals the full truth: the Republic's founders destroyed the Archive to seize their gates, then framed the Concord's ancestors. Both sides have been fighting a lie. Xanthe understands why his original died — and what broadcasting this will cost everyone.

chapters.title: Voss's Choice
chapters.summary: POV Admiral Voss. Arriving at the Drift, Voss receives final confirmation of the cover-up from her own intelligence chief — the man who ordered her to burn the gate. She arrests him instead, seizes his evidence, and turns her fleet toward the gate. Not redemption yet. Defection.

chapters.title: Three Fleets, One Window
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. The jump window opens in six hours. Concord holds the gate exterior, Voss's defecting squadron is inbound, and Republic loyalists pursue them all. Xanthe's plan: broadcast the unedited testament through the gate's own array — visible to every ship in the system simultaneously.

chapters.title: Reyes at the Airlock
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Concord boarders breach the vault. Xanthe faces Reyes directly and offers her the raw archive — every document, unedited, including Concord's own complicity in early atrocities. She hesitates between the war she wants and the truth she fears. Her second-in-command doesn't hesitate, and opens fire.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe, climax. Wounded, with the vault collapsing around them, Xanthe speaks the Archive's testament in its own dead language — live, system-wide, through the gate. Voss's squadron holds off the loyalists. Reyes, having seen the full record, orders Concord guns silent. The truth goes out on every channel.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Truth
chapters.summary: POV ensemble. Cease-fire spreads ship by ship as crews absorb the broadcast. Voss surrenders her fleet to neutral arbitration; Reyes resigns command. The gate stands open — not as a weapon, but as a library. Casualties are counted, including friends among the Concord dead.

chapters.title: Nakamura, Signed
chapters.summary: POV Xanthe. Recovering aboard a salvaged hull, Xanthe signs his own name — not the original's — to the formal testimony. He visits the memorial wall where his original is listed, and adds no second line. He was never a duplicate of a dead man; he was the one who finished the sentence.

chapters.title: First Jump
chapters.summary: POV Pip, closing frame. The rebuilt crew — Xanthe, Dessa, Ruel earning his keep, Pip at navigation — prepares to take a small ship of scholars through the gate on the first peaceful crossing in two centuries. Xanthe translates the Archive's farewell inscription aloud. They jump together into the unknown.
